newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Sept CPI up 0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. Sept CPI up 0.3 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent, following a 0.1-percent increase in August. The core rate, which excludes volatile food and energy items, was also up 0.3 percent.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey had expected 0.3-percent rises in both the overall and core rates.
WADLO BEST, SENIOR ECONOMIST, BZW GOVERNMENT SECURITIES INC: "The (Treasury) market got as-expected numbers. The market is going to rally ... It's just a relief."

Best continued: "When you look at the details, everything came in as expected ... A little bit of good news was that energy was flat, but the uptick in aircraft and apparel was expected; all of these things were expected. There's really no surprise in the numbers.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER REYNOLDS INC: "It's right in line with what the (Treasury) market was looking for. That's why an initial reaction is a little relief buying in the market right now, that you didn't get something stronger than expected."

Flanagan added: "We got a warning from BLS (Bureau of Labor Statistics) officials that this could be a little higher than what was envisioned. But all in all, I think the market will be satisfied that inflation continues to remain relatively subdued."

MATTHEW ALEXY, CHIEF MARKET STRATEGIST, CS FIRST BOSTON CORP: "This is very similar to the PPI nature (because) you have numbers that are sort of counter balancing each other. That 0.3 percent is an upside miss on the CPI and we're all right on the inflation front. These numbers are fine."

MARILYN SCHAJA, MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST, DONALDSON, LUFKIN AND JENRETTE SECURITIES CORP: "The numbers are very constructive in that the overall number was only up 0.3 and the core was up 0.3. If you average out September and August the number is only up 0.2 percent.

"There were some extraneous one-time events in this number: airline fares being up 2.9 percent and tobacco prices being up 0.7 percent ... The apparel reversing a little bit of the negative 1.4 percent the prior month. Even with those factors the number is only up 0.3 percent.
"The bond (market) should react constructively in my opinion. The market feared a worse number and I think it should do better on these statistics," she added.
